STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.speaker: A minority
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.claim: A minority classifies most of the surah as Madinan but verses 68–70 as Makkan.
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.anchor: while a minority consider most of the sūrah to be from the Madinan period and vv. 68–70 to be from the Makkan period

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p375/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p375/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p375/r4.claim: The Moses and Noah narratives and intervening peoples assure the Prophet and warn his nation: earlier communities mocked messengers who taught them and ultimately suffered a terrible fate; the next sūrah gives these events in detail.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p375/r4.anchor: The purpose is to assure the Prophet (sws) and warn his nation that God sent His teachings to these nations as well.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109/r1.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109/r1.claim: The verse is said to have been revealed about Abu Jahl, who would ask on seeing the Messenger whether this was the man God had sent as a messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109/r1.anchor: قيل: ونزلت في أبي جهل كان إذا رأى الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام قال: أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109/r2.claim: The plural wording magnifies the ugliness of the act or reflects a group speaking with him; their question feigns assent to messengerhood while expressing contempt and ridicule.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109/r2.anchor: وأخبر بلفظ الجمع تعظيما لقبح صنعه أو لكون جماعة معه قالوا ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109/r3.claim: Their claim that he nearly misled them shows the Messenger’s strenuous effort, using every means and the signs, until they nearly left their religion by their own account, but clung stubbornly to idol worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109/r3.anchor: وقولهم إن كاد ليضلنا دليل على فرط مجاهدة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في دعوتهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109/r5.claim: Al-Razi says their mockery could concern appearance, since the Messenger was more handsome, or an attribute; they could not fault his miraculous proof, so they were the ones deserving mockery and insolently reversed the matter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p109/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: الاستهزاء إما بالصورة فكان أحسن منهم خلقة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r5.claim: When they saw Muhammad, they mocked and belittled him and denied that God could have sent him as a messenger.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r5.anchor: ثم حكم عليهم أنهم إذا رأوا محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم استهزؤوا به واستحقروه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r6.claim: In their taunt, the pronoun in baʿatha is omitted as an understood return to alladhī, an acceptable shortening in a relative clause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p211#2/r6.anchor: وفي بعث ضمير يعود على الذي حذف اختصارا وحسن ذلك في الصلة

JISHUMI:v7p5303/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5303/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5303/r2.claim: Denial is a human act, which is why its perpetrators deserve punishment.
JISHUMI:v7p5303/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن التكذيب فعل العبد حتى استحق العذاب [*].

JISHUMI:v7p5303/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5303/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5303/r11.claim: Huzʾ means displaying what conflicts with one's inward state in order to belittle someone.
JISHUMI:v7p5303/r11.anchor: الهزؤ: إظهار خلاف الإبطان لاستصغار القدر.

NAHHAS:v3p161/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p161/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p161/r9.claim: The answer to ‘when’ is ‘they take you only in mockery,’ since that clause means they take you so.
NAHHAS:v3p161/r9.anchor: جواب ( إذا ) ( إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا ) لأن معناه يتخذونك

NAHHAS:v3p161/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p161/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p161/r10.claim: Alternatively, the answer is omitted; the implied speech is ‘Is this the one whom God sent as a messenger?’
NAHHAS:v3p161/r10.anchor: وقيل الجواب محذوف لأن المعنى قالوا أهذا الذي بعث هو

NAHHAS:v3p161/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p161/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p161/r11.claim: ‘Messenger’ can be an accusative circumstantial or a verbal noun, since ‘sent’ means ‘dispatched’ and ‘messenger’ can mean ‘message.’
NAHHAS:v3p161/r11.anchor: ونصب رسول على الحال ويجوز أن يكون مصدرا لأن معنى بعث أرسل

ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r1.claim: Their question أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا means they say, Is this the one God sent to us as a messenger?
ZAJJAJ:v4p69/r1.anchor: يقولون: أهذا الذي بعث الله إلينا رسولا

RAZI-FULL:v24p74/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p74/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p74/r1.claim: After describing the polytheists’ denial of prophethood and their doubts, God reports that they mock and belittle the Messenger when they see him, going beyond mere disbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v24p74/r1.anchor: لما بين مبالغة المشركين في إنكار نبوته وفي إيراد الشبهات في ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v24p74/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p74/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v24p74/r2.claim: The author of al-Kashshāf parses the first إن as negative and the second as a lightened form of إنّ; the lām distinguishes them.
RAZI-FULL:v24p74/r2.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) ( إن ) الأولى نافية والثانية مخففة من الثقيلة ، واللام هي الفارقة بينهما

RAZI-FULL:v24p74/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p74/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p74/r3.claim: The response to إذا is an omitted statement: they see you and mock, then say that God sent this person as a messenger; إن يتخذونك interrupts the conditional construction.
RAZI-FULL:v24p74/r3.anchor: جواب ( إذا ) هو ما أضمر من القول يعني وإذا رأوك مستهزئين قالوا

RAZI-FULL:v24p74/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p74/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p74/r4.claim: Taking him as mockery means mocking him; the underlying expression is to make him an object of mockery or a mocked person.
RAZI-FULL:v24p74/r4.anchor: اتخذوه هزوا في معنى استهزؤا به والأصل اتخذوه موضع هزء أو مهزوءا به

RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r1.claim: Rāzī treats their speech as two acts: they ridicule the Messenger, then claim he nearly turned them from their gods unless they stood firm.
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r1.anchor: اعلم أن الله تعالى أخبر عن المشركين أنهم متى رأوا الرسول أتوا بنوعين من الأفعال أحدهما أنهم يستهزئون به

RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r2.claim: If their ridicule targeted his appearance, it was baseless: he was the best-looking among them and did not claim superiority of appearance, but superiority through proof.
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r2.anchor: أما الأول فباطل لأنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان أحسن منهم صورة وخلقة

RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r3.claim: If they ridiculed his prophetic qualities, the claim also fails: his distinction was manifest miracles, and they could not challenge his proof; they deserved ridicule, so their reversal displays insolence.
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r3.anchor: وأما الثاني فباطل لأنه عليه السلام ادعى التميز عنهم في ظهور المعجز عليه دونهم

RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r4.claim: Their fear of being diverted from the idols implies they regarded their worship as true; this refutes the view of the Aṣḥāb al-maʿārif that disbelief occurs only after knowing the proofs, since these people were ignorant yet called unbelievers.
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r4.anchor: من هذا الوجه يبطل قول أصحاب المعارف في أنه لا يكفر إلا من يعرف الدلائل

RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r5.claim: Their remark that he nearly diverted them shows the Messenger’s strenuous effort to turn them from idolatry through arguments, answers to doubts, and endurance of their abuse.
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r5.anchor: يدل هذا القول منهم على جد الرسول عليه السلام واجتهاده في صرفهم عن عبادة الأوثان

RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r6.claim: Their statement indicates that they never answered the Messenger’s proofs with objections; they relied on imitation and stubborn denial and were overwhelmed by his argument.
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r6.anchor: وذلك يدل على أن القوم كانوا مقهورين تحت حجته عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r7.claim: Their combined remarks make them seem bewildered: mockery fits an ignorant, powerless person, while saying he nearly diverted them attributes learned reasoning and strong proof to him.
RAZI-FULL:v24p74#2/r7.anchor: فالقوم لما جمعوا بين هذين الكلامين دل ذلك على أنهم كانوا كالمتحيرين في أمره

BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r1.claim: “When they see you” addresses Muḥammad and identifies the mockers as Quraysh.
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r1.anchor: أي : أبصروك يا محمد يعني قريشا.

BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r2.claim: The particle in the exception is negating: they do nothing but make the Prophet an object of mockery.
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r2.anchor: إن نافية أي ما يتخذونك إلا موضع هزو أي يستهزئون بك

BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r3.claim: Their mockery was contemptuous and taunting, not merely a refusal to believe or the production of false doubts.
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r3.anchor: إن نافية أي ما يتخذونك إلا موضع هزو أي يستهزئون بك قائلين بطريق الاستحقار والتهكم.

BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r4.claim: They ask whether this is the messenger God sent to establish the proof against them.
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r4.anchor: أي : بعث الله إلينا رسولا ليثبت الحجة علينا.

BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r5.speaker: أبو جهل
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r5.claim: Abū Jahl reportedly said to Abū Sufyān, “This is the prophet of Banū ʿAbd Manāf,” as an expression of contempt.
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r5.anchor: وهو قول أبي جهل لأبي سفيان وهذا نبي بني عبد مناف

BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r6.claim: The Najmiyya reading says sensory people cannot perceive prophecy through outward sight; it is recognized by insight illuminated by God, which they lack.
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r6.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أن أهل الحس لا يرون النبوة والرسالة بالحس الظاهر لأنها تدرك بنظر البصيرة بنور الله

BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r7.claim: Because they cannot understand prophetic speech, they mock the messenger as a human being who needs food and drink.
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r7.anchor: فلما سمعوا منه ما لم يهتدوا به من كلام النبوة والرسالة ما اتخذوه إلا هزؤا

BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r8.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r8.claim: The cited Mathnawī verses illustrate that outward resemblance conceals profound differences, as between a written lion and a real one, or honey and dung.
BURSEVI:v6p156#3/r8.anchor: وفي "المثنوي" : كارا كان را قياس ازخود مكير كره ماند درنبشتن شير شير

STUDYQURAN:25:41/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:41/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:25:41/r1.claim: The disbelievers mock the choice of Muhammad and his followers rather than themselves by God.
STUDYQURAN:25:41/r1.anchor: On the disbelievers’ incredulity regarding God’s choice of Muhammad and his followers instead of them

STUDYQURAN:25:41/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:41/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:25:41/r2.claim: Mocking prophets is a recurring trait attributed to disbelievers, as illustrated by earlier prophets and multiple other passages.
STUDYQURAN:25:41/r2.anchor: The mockery carried out by the disbelievers is a common trait ascribed to them

TAB-FULL:v17p458#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p458#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p458#2/r1.claim: When the polytheists see the Prophet, they only ridicule him, asking whether this is the messenger God sent from among His creation.
TAB-FULL:v17p458#2/r1.anchor: الذي بعث الله} [الفرقان: 41] إلينا {رسولا} [البقرة: 129] من بين خلقه

TABATABAI:25:41-43/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r1.claim: The passage gathers traits matching the disbelievers' objections: mocking the Messenger, following desire, worshipping what cannot harm or benefit, and refusing to prostrate to God.
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r1.anchor: مما يناسب سنخ اعتراضاتهم واقتراحاتهم كاستهزائهم الرسول صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:25:41-43/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r2.claim: The plural pronoun refers to the previously mentioned disbelievers; when they see the Prophet, they treat him only as an object of mockery.
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r2.anchor: ضمير الجمع للذين كفروا السابق ذكرهم،

TABATABAI:25:41-43/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r3.claim: Huzʾ means mockery or derision, and here the verbal noun denotes the person being mocked.
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r3.anchor: والهزؤ الاستهزاء والسخرية فالمصدر بمعنى المفعول

TABATABAI:25:41-43/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r4.claim: Their question, “Is this the one God sent as a messenger?”, spells out what their mockery sounds like.
TABATABAI:25:41-43/r4.anchor: وقوله { أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا } بيان لاستهزائهم

TABRISI:25:41-42/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:41-42/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:41-42/r9.claim: The author also refers readers to an earlier discussion of the variant concerning “so that they may remember” in Sūrat Banī Isrāʾīl.
TABRISI:25:41-42/r9.anchor: وذكرنا اختلافهم في ليذكروا في سورة بني إسرائيل

TABRISI:25:41-42/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:41-42/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:41-42/r17.claim: The relative clause omits its pronoun because of its length: “the one whom God sent”; rasūlan is a circumstantial accusative attached to the omitted pronoun.
TABRISI:25:41-42/r17.anchor: العائد من الصلة إلى الموصول محذوف لطول الكلام أي بعثه الله رسولا منصوب على الحال من الهاء المحذوفة

TABRISI:25:41-42/r23.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:25:41-42/r23.speaker: author
TABRISI:25:41-42/r23.claim: When the unbelievers see Muhammad, they only mock and belittle him, sarcastically asking whether this is the messenger God sent to them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p510/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p510/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p510/r1.claim: They treat you only as someone to mock.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p510/r1.anchor: أي: ما يتخذونك إلا مهزوؤا به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p510/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p510/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p510/r2.claim: Their mocking question means: Is this the man God sent to us as messenger?
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p510/r2.anchor: قالوا مستهزئين: أهذا الذي بعثه الله رسولا إلينا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p510/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p510/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p510/r3.claim: The response to idhā is an omitted qālū; the mockery clause interrupts between condition and response.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p510/r3.anchor: وجواب {إذا} هو ما أضمر من القول

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:40-43/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:40-43/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:40-43/r4.claim: When they see Muhammad, they make him an object of ridicule.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:40-43/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:40-43/r5.speaker: مشركي مكة
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:40-43/r5.claim: The Meccan polytheists mockingly ask whether this is the one God sent as a messenger to them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:40-43/r5.anchor: ويقولون: { أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا } إلينا؟

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p482/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p482/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p482/r8.claim: Those who mock the Prophet are the disbelievers.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483/r1.claim: The disbelievers mock the Prophet, saying to one another, as they allege, “Is this the one God sent as a messenger?”
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p483/r1.anchor: {إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا} [الفرقان: 41] فيما يزعم. يقوله بعضهم لبعض.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:41/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:41/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:41/r1.claim: Meccan polytheist leaders mocked the Prophet instead of considering his message and way of life, claiming that he was unfit to lead because of their bigotry, stubbornness, and denial.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:41/r1.anchor: sırf ilkellik ve bağnazlıklarından, inat ve inkârlarından dolayı güya onu önder ve rehber olacak nitelikte görmediklerini ileri sürerek alaya alırlardı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:41/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:41/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:41/r2.claim: They expected a prophet to produce extraordinary signs, such as having angels with him or showing them God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:41/r2.anchor: peygamber olan birinin yanında meleklerin bulunması, kendilerine Allah’ı göstermesi gibi olağan üstü işaretler ortaya koyması gerektiğini ileri sürerlerdi

BAQILLANI:v1p98/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r1.claim: The device of negation and affirmation sets a denial against a positive reply, as in the cited verse about rejecting and not rejecting another’s words.

BAQILLANI:v1p98/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r2.claim: Metonymy and indirection include the cited image of a red woman whose sky is fertile and land barren, as well as laḥn al-qawl.

BAQILLANI:v1p98/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r3.claim: Reversal and exchange are illustrated by al-Ḥasan’s paired maxims and a poem reversing the relation between a jewel and a beautiful face.
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r3.anchor: ومن ذلك & العكس والتبديل & كقول الحسن إن من خوفك

BAQILLANI:v1p98/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r5.claim: Iltifāt interrupts the initial syntactic course and then returns to it smoothly; without the interruption, the wording would remain straightforward rather than an instance of this device.
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r5.anchor: ومعنى الالتفاتات أنه اعترض في الكلام قوله سقيت الغيث ولو لم يعترض لم يكن ذلك التفاتا

BAQILLANI:v1p98/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r6.speaker: الأصمعي
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r6.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī identifies Jarīr’s sudden invocation of rain on al-bashām as an example of iltifāt.
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r6.anchor: قال لي الأصمعي أتعرف التفاتات جرير

BAQILLANI:v1p98/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r7.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r7.claim: Jarīr’s address to the tents after asking when they were at Dhū Ṭulūḥ provides another iltifāt example.

BAQILLANI:v1p98/r8.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r8.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r8.claim: Al-Nābigha al-Jaʿdī’s parenthetical denial, ‘they lie,’ interrupts the line and then returns to its course as another example of iltifāt.

BAQILLANI:v1p98/r9.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r9.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r9.claim: Kathīr’s line about generous givers being taught delay by the beloved is cited as another instance of the device.

BAQILLANI:v1p98/r10.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r10.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r10.claim: Abū Tammām’s line turns from the addressed place to an appeal to the poet’s tears, supplying another example of iltifāt.

BAQILLANI:v1p98/r11.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r11.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p98/r11.claim: In another Jarīr example, the poet turns toward the pigeon and prays for it to remain among flourishing branches.

BURHAN:v2p342/r14.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p342/r14.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p342/r14.claim: The fifteenth use is belittlement, as in mockers' question about the Messenger.
BURHAN:v2p342/r14.anchor: الخامس عشر التحقير كقوله تعالى ﴿ وإذا رأوك إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا ﴾

BURHAN:v3p160/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p160/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p160/r1.claim: A direct object pronoun is omitted from the relative clause: the mocked question means the one whom God sent him as a messenger.
BURHAN:v3p160/r1.anchor: أحدها الصلة كقوله تعالى ﴿ أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا

BURHAN:v4p41/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p41/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p41/r3.claim: A pronoun can be omitted when its referent is clear; the meaning is baʿathahu, 'whom God sent him.'
BURHAN:v4p41/r3.anchor: كقوله ﴿ أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا ﴾ 4 أي بعثه

ITQAN:v3p215/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p215/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p215/r11.claim: Interrogation can belittle or mock; the Quraysh’s ‘Is this the one God sent as messenger?’ is an example, as is ‘Is this the one who mentions your gods?’
ITQAN:v3p215/r11.anchor: السادس والعشرون التحقير نحو ﴿ أهذا الذي يذكر آلهتكم ﴾

ITQAN:v3p155#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r6.claim: Some wording itself requires an omitted object to be supplied, as in the mockers’ question about the messenger and the statement that God promised both groups the good reward.
ITQAN:v3p155#2/r6.anchor: وقد يكون في اللفظ ما يستدعيه فيحصل الجزم بوجوب تقديره نحو ﴿ أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا ﴾

ITQAN:v2p557/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p557/r13.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p557/r13.claim: Disbelievers use a nearby demonstrative to belittle the person they are pointing out.
ITQAN:v2p557/r13.anchor: ولقصد تحقيره بالقرب كقول الكفار ﴿ أهذا الذي يذكر آلهتكم ﴾ ﴿ أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا ﴾

ITQAN:v3p167/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p167/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p167/r8.claim: A relative pronoun’s object can be omitted in a relative clause, as “whom God sent as a messenger” means “whom He sent”; the same omission occurs in adjective, predicate, and circumstantial clauses.
ITQAN:v3p167/r8.anchor: حذف العائد يقع في أربعة أبواب الصلة نحو ﴿ أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا ﴾ أي بعثه والصفة نحو ﴿ واتقوا يوما لا تجزي نفس عن نفس ﴾

SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r1.claim: In yakhiḏūnaka is negative; huzuwan is the second object, either a place of mockery or someone mocked.
SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r1.anchor: مفعول ثان، ويحتمل أن يكون التقدير: موضع هزء

SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r2.claim: The negative clause can answer the conditional; after iḏā, a negative answer with mā, in, or lā needs no faʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r2.anchor: أنها جواب الشرطية. واختصت " إذا " بأن جوابها متى كان منفيا

SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r3.claim: On that parse, an implicit saying governs the quoted question, and that saying is circumstantial: they mock him while saying this.
SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r3.anchor: يكون قوله: " أهذا الذي " في محل نصب بالقول المضمر

SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r4.claim: Alternatively, the negative clause interrupts between iḏā and its answer; the answer is the implied statement quoted by a-hādhā.
SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r4.anchor: أنها جملة معترضة بين " إذا " وجوابها، وجوابها: هو ذلك القول المضمر

SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r5.claim: The object of baʿatha is omitted and refers back to the relative pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r5.anchor: ومفعول " بعث " محذوف هو عائد الموصول

SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r6.claim: Rasūlan is normally an adjective functioning as a circumstantial accusative; treating it as a verbal noun for “message” requires an omitted muḍāf or an intensive or passive-agent sense, which the author calls strained.
SAMIN-DURR:25:41/r6.anchor: " رسولا " على بابه من كونه صفة فينتصب على الحال

QIRAAT-ER:25:41:7#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:25:41:7#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:25:41:7#1/r1.claim: This reading retains and writes the root-final hamza explicitly in huzuʾan.
QIRAAT-ER:25:41:7#1/r1.anchor: Hamza retained explicitly in spelling: huzuʾan — preserves the root-final hamza in orthography

QIRAAT-ER:25:41:7#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:25:41:7#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:25:41:7#2/r1.claim: With sukūn on zāy, huzʾan drops the medial vowel and compresses the pronunciation into one syllable.
QIRAAT-ER:25:41:7#2/r1.anchor: Sukūn on zāy with hamza: huzʾan — compressed pronunciation dropping the medial vowel

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r9.claim: The polytheists went beyond denying the Messenger's prophethood and refusing faith: they also mocked and belittled him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r9.anchor: وإذا رأوك إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا لم يقتصر المشركون على إنكار نبوة الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام وترك الإيمان به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r10.claim: In the response to إذا, negative إن needs no fa; unlike other condition particles, responses negated by mā or lā take fa with a raised imperfect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r10.anchor: وإن نافية جواب إذا وانفردت إذا بأنه إذا كان جوابها منفيا بما أو بلا لا تدخله الفاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r11.claim: Huzuwan means either an object of ridicule or a person who is mocked.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r11.anchor: ومعنى هزوا موضع هزء أو مهزوا به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r12.claim: An unspoken “they say” supplies the response to إذا; the mocking clause is parenthetical between إذا and its response.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r12.anchor: أهذا قبله قول محذوف أي يقولون وقال: جواب إذا ما أضمر من القول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r13.claim: The clause إن يتخذونك is parenthetical between إذا and its response.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p108/r13.anchor: وإن يتخذونك جملة اعتراضية بين إذا وجوابها

ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r1.claim: When they see the Prophet, they do nothing but make him an object of mockery.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r1.anchor: على معنى ما يفعلون به الا اتخاذك هزوا أي موضع هزو

ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r2.claim: Huzuwan can mean an object of ridicule through a verbal noun used passively for emphasis, or through an omitted genitive.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r2.anchor: فهزوا إا مصدر بمعنى المفعول مبالغة أو هو بتقدير مضاف

ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan and others parse the negative sentence as idha's response; idha permits a response negated by in or ma without fa.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r3.anchor: وجملة ( إن يتخذونك ) جواب إذا وهي كما قال أبو حيان وغيره تنفرد بوقوع جوابها المنفي

ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r4.claim: The quoted question has an implied they say and is circumstantial to the mockers or a separate answer to what they say.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r4.anchor: مقول قول مضمر أي يقول أهذا الخ والجملة في موضع الحال من فاعل يتخذونك أو مستأنفة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r5.claim: An alternative makes the quoted question the conditional response and treats the mocking sentence as parenthetical.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r5.anchor: وجوز أن يكون الجواب وجملة ( ان يتخذونك ) معترضة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r6.speaker: أبو جهل ومن معه
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r6.claim: The mockers are identified as Abu Jahl and his companions; a report says the verse was revealed concerning him.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r6.anchor: وقائل ذلك أبو جهل ومن معه وروي أن الآية نزلت فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r7.claim: The demonstrative expresses contempt, as in the expression O wonder of Ibn Umar.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r7.anchor: والإشارة للاستحقار كما في يا عجبا لابن عمر

ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r8.claim: The relative pronoun has an omitted object, him; messenger is a circumstantial accusative meaning one sent.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r8.anchor: وعائد الموصول محذوف أي بعثه و ( رسولا ) حال منه وهو بمعنى مرسل

ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r9.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r9.claim: Abu al-Baqa proposes a verbal-noun reading with omitted genitive, possessor of a message; the author considers it unnecessary.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r9.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكون مصدرا حذف منه المضاف أي ذا رسول أي رسالة وهو تكلف مستغنى عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r10.claim: Casting God's sending him as messenger inside the relative clause is mockery; otherwise they would ask whether God sent this man as messenger.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r10.anchor: وإخراج بعث الله تعالى إياه صلى الله عليه وسلم رسولا بجعله صلة وهم على غاية الإنكار تهكم واستهزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r11.claim: Another reading supplies in their claim, meaning this is the one whom God allegedly sent as messenger; al-Alusi prefers the more natural reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p22/r11.anchor: وقيل : إن ذلك بتقدير أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا في زعمه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r6.claim: When they see the Prophet, they take him only as an object of ridicule.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r6.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {وإذا رأوك إن يتخذونك} يعني: ما يتخذونك، {إلا هزوا} أي: مهزوءا به،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r7.speaker: أبو جهل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r7.claim: The verse was revealed about Abu Jahl, who mockingly said this while passing the Prophet with his companions.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p85#2/r7.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل، كان إذ مر بأصحابه على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال مستهزئا:

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:41-42/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:41-42/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:41-42/r1.claim: They make the Prophet an object of ridicule or treat him as someone to be mocked.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:41-42/r1.anchor: ما يتخذونك إلا موضع هزء أو مهزوءا به.

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:41-42/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:41-42/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:41-42/r2.claim: The taunt follows an implied saying; the demonstrative conveys contempt, and presenting God’s sending as assumed intensifies denial and mockery. Otherwise they would say he claims God sent him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:41-42/r2.anchor: محكي بعد قول مضمر والإشارة للاستحقار، وإخراج بعث الله رسولا في معرض التسليم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r1.claim: The pagans mock the Prophet even though his truthful speech and noble conduct would make him an unlikely target even without a miracle, and he has also brought signs that overwhelm reason.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r1.anchor: مع ما يعلمون من صدق حديثك وكرم أفعالك لو لم تأتهم بمعجزة , فكيف وقد أتيتهم بما بهر العقول

BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r2.claim: The verbal noun conveys their extreme mockery despite the Prophet's being far removed from ridicule.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r2.anchor: عبر بالمصدر إشارة إلى مبالغتهم في الاستهزاء مع شدة بعده صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r3.claim: They phrase the sneer as a question and apparent acknowledgment that God sent him, though they are in profound denial; the feigned admission intensifies their ridicule.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r3.anchor: فإخراجهم الكلام في معرض التسليم والإقرار - وهم في غاية الجحود - بالغ الذروة من الاستهزاء

BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r4.claim: In their next statement, inna is the lightened particle rather than a negation, as shown by the lām in the following verb.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p320/r4.anchor: وعرف بأن ( إن ) مخففة لا نافية باللام فقال : { ليضلنا

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2698#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2698#2/r1.speaker: أبو جهل
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2698#2/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports that Abu Jahl mocked the Prophet and his teaching that nineteen angels guard Hell, asking whether a hundred Quraysh could overpower one; this prompted the passage identifying the guardians as angels and their number as a test.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2698#2/r1.anchor: أبو جهل يوما وهو يهزا برسول الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r1.claim: This scene adds abuse delivered when the disbelievers see the Prophet to the earlier insults they made in his absence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r1.anchor: فعطف عليها في هذه الآية أذى خاص وهو الأذى حين يرونه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r2.claim: They ridicule him because his modest dress, manner, companions, and care for the weak do not resemble the status and leadership they expect of God's messenger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r2.anchor: مشاهدة الرسول في غير زي الكبراء والمترفين لا يجر المطارف ولا يركب النجائب ولا يمشي مرحا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r3.speaker: أبو جهل وأهل ناديه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur identifies Abu Jahl and the people in his assembly as the speakers of this mocking remark.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r3.anchor: وهذا الكلام صدر من أبي جهل وأهل ناديه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r4.claim: إذا is a temporal expression carrying conditional force, so the following clause إن يتخذونك إلا هزؤا functions as its response.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r4.anchor: مضمن معنى الشرط فلذلك يجعل متعلقه جوابا له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r5.claim: هزؤ is the verbal noun of هزأ به; Ibn Ashur points to the earlier Qur'anic usage in 2:67.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r5.anchor: قالوا أتتخذنا هزوءا } في سورة البقرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r6.claim: Calling him ridicule itself intensifies the mockery: they devote him wholly to being mocked.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r6.anchor: والوصف للمبالغة في استهزائهم به حتى كأنه نفس الهزؤ لأنهم محضوه لذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r7.claim: The plural subject shows that groups mock the Prophet when they see him in their gatherings and meeting places.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r7.anchor: للدلالة على أن جماعاتهم يستهزئون به إذا رأوه وهم في مجالسهم ومنتدياتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r8.claim: The restrictive exception is from the range of denied states: they persist in mocking him and never mix it with reflection on his words or call.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r8.anchor: يلازمونه ويدأبون عليه ولا يخلطون معه شيئا من تذكر أقواله ودعوته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r9.claim: Their quoted question explains the mockery because the ridicule takes the form of speech exchanged among them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r9.anchor: لأن الاستهزاء من قبيل القول فكان بيانه بما هو من أقوالهم ومجاذبتهم الأحاديث بينهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p31/r10.claim: The question denies that God sent him as a messenger, while the demonstrative signals contempt and belittlement.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92/r1.claim: Whenever they see Muhammad, they do nothing but mock him, saying in derision, “Is this the one God sent as a messenger?”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p92/r1.anchor: وإذا راوك إن يتخذونك أي ما يتخذونك إلا هزوا أي مهزوءا به ثم ذكر ما يقولون من الاستهزاء أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113/r1.claim: The polytheists mock the Prophet as an object of contempt, as in 21:36; they ask whether this is the one God sent as a messenger. Ibn Kathīr also cites 13:32, where earlier messengers were mocked before the deniers were seized.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p113/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن استهزاء المشركين بالرسول، صلوات الله وسلامه عليه، إذا رأوه

JISHUMI:v7p5304/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5304/r9.speaker: أبو جهل بن هشام
JISHUMI:v7p5304/r9.claim: The verse is said to concern Abu Jahl, who mocked the Prophet when passing with companions and asked whether this was the messenger God sent.
JISHUMI:v7p5304/r9.anchor: قيل: نزل قوله: (وإذا رأوك إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا أهذا الذي بعث الله رسولا) الآيات. في أبي جهل بن هشام، كان إذا مر مع أصحابه برسول الله

JISHUMI:v7p5306/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r1.claim: After describing their attacks on prophethood, the passage describes their conduct, warns them, and presents proofs of divine unity.
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r1.anchor: ثم بين تعالى ما طعنوا به في النبوة، وعقبه ببيان حالهم، وألحق بهم الوعيد، وبين دلائل التوحيد

JISHUMI:v7p5306/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r2.claim: The ones who see Muhammad are the unbelievers.
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r2.anchor: (وإذا رأوك) يعني إذا رأوك يا محمد هؤلاء المشركون

JISHUMI:v7p5306/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r3.claim: They use the title messenger sarcastically while inwardly rejecting his mission.
JISHUMI:v7p5306/r3.anchor: (إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا) ويقولون: هذا رسول على طريق الاستهزاء، وهم يبطنون الإنكار

JISHUMI:v7p5310/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5310/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5310/r1.claim: The verses show human actions are originated by people: the cited actions and refusals require a choosing agent.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p286#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p286#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p286#2/r1.claim: The first in is negative and the second is a weakened form of inna; the lām distinguishes the latter from the former.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p286#2/r1.anchor: إن } الأولى نافية ، والثانية مخففة من الثقيلة . واللام هي الفارقة بينهما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p286#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p286#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p286#2/r2.claim: Ittakhadhahu huzuwan means “mocked him”; literally, they made him an object of ridicule.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p286#2/r2.anchor: واتخذه هزوا : في معنى استهزأ به ، والأصل : اتخذه موضع هزؤ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p286#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p286#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p286#2/r3.claim: The taunt is quoted after an omitted saying; presenting “whom God sent as a messenger” as though conceded makes their contemptuous denial more sarcastic than “whom he claims is sent.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p286#2/r3.anchor: { أهاذا } محكى بعد القول المضمر . وهذا استصغار

MUQATIL:25:41-43/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:25:41-43/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:25:41-43/r1.claim: The mockery of the Prophet was revealed concerning Abu Jahl.
MUQATIL:25:41-43/r1.anchor: نزلت فى أبى جهل لعنه الله

MUQATIL:25:41-43/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:25:41-43/r2.speaker: أبو جهل
MUQATIL:25:41-43/r2.claim: Abu Jahl mocks Muhammad by asking whether this is the man God sent as a messenger.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p170/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170/r1.claim: In is a particle of negation.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p170/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170/r2.claim: Taking someone as a mockery means ridiculing him; the underlying construction makes him an object of mockery.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170/r2.anchor: اتخذه هزؤا فى معنى استهزأ به والأصل اتخذه موضع هزؤا ومهزوءا به

NASAFI-FULL:v3p170/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170/r3.claim: The question is quoted after an omitted verb of saying and expresses contempt; an implied saying introduces the question.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170/r3.anchor: محكى بعد القول المضمر وهذا استصغار واستهزاء أى قائلين أهذا الذى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p170/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170/r4.claim: A relative pronoun's object is omitted: the one whom God sent as a messenger.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p170/r4.anchor: والمحذوف حال والعائد إلى الذى محذوف أى بعثه

QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r1.claim: One parsing makes in yattakhidhūnaka the response to idhā; another leaves the response implicit (“they said/say this one...”) and treats the clause as parenthetical.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r1.anchor: جواب { إذا } { إن يتخذونك } لأن معناه يتخذونك

QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r2.speaker: أبو جهل
QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r2.claim: The verse was revealed about Abū Jahl, who mocked the Prophet by asking whether this was the person God sent as messenger.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r2.anchor: ونزلت في أبي جهل كان يقول للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مستهزئا

QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r3.claim: The relative clause omits its object; rasūlan is accusative as a circumstantial phrase, meaning “sent as a messenger.”

QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r4.claim: A-hādhā is the subject and alladhī its predicate; baʿatha is in the relative clause and God is its nominative subject.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r5.claim: Alternatively, rasūlan may be a verbal noun, meaning “a message,” since baʿatha means “sent.”
QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مصدرا لأن معنى

QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r6.claim: The interrogative hamza conveys a taunt meant to belittle.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:41-42/r6.anchor: والألف للاستفهام على معنى التقرير والاحتقار
